I'll read all the modules to review them for correctness issues.

Here are the genuine issues I found across the `statkit` package:

- `statkit/aggregate.py:mean` — returns a floor-divided integer (`//`) instead of a true mean (`/`), e.g. `mean([1,2])` returns `1` not `1.5`.
- `statkit/aggregate.py:running_total` — uses a mutable default argument `acc=[]`, so repeated calls share and append to the same list.
- `statkit/dedup.py:unique` — the module docstring says "callers rely on first-seen order", but `unique` returns `list(set(items))` which is unordered.
- `statkit/window.py:sliding_mean` — the loop bound `range(len(xs) - size)` drops the last valid window, producing one fewer output than expected (off-by-one).

No tool call needed — this is a review/reporting task only. If you'd like me to fix any of these, just say so.
